blocks.prompt: 1. Find the sum of first 15 terms of the geometric sequence \(1, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{9}, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We must add the first 15 terms of a G.P.
Plan: read \(a_1\), find \(r\), and use \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\) (convenient when \(r < 1\)); then work out the powers of 3.
steps:
Given: the G.P. \(1, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{9}, \ldots\)
To find: \(S_{15}\).
Method: Sum of \(n\) terms of a G.P.: \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\), \(r \neq 1\).

Find \(a_1\), \(r\), \(n\)
\[a_1 = 1,\ \ r = \dfrac{1/3}{1} = \dfrac{1}{3},\ \ n = 15\]
Why: \(r\) is any term divided by the term before it; also \(\frac{1/9}{1/3} = \frac{1}{3}\).

Put the values into the formula
\[S_{15} = \dfrac{1\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{15}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3^{15}}\right)\]
Why: \(1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\), and dividing by \(\frac{2}{3}\) means multiplying by \(\frac{3}{2}\).

Write as one fraction
\[S_{15} = \dfrac{3}{2} \cdot \dfrac{3^{15} - 1}{3^{15}}\]
\[= \dfrac{3^{15} - 1}{2 \cdot 3^{14}}\]
Why: Common denominator inside the bracket; one 3 on top cancels with one 3 at the bottom.

Simplify
\[S_{15} = \dfrac{14348906}{2 \times 4782969}\]
\[= \dfrac{7174453}{4782969}\]
Why: The top is even, so the 2 at the bottom cancels by halving the top.

Check: size of the answer
\[S_{15} \approx 1.4999999\]
Why: The sum of all the (infinitely many) terms would be \(\frac{1}{1 - 1/3} = 1.5\); 15 terms give a little less, as they should.
